title: Building game UIs
author: Prestigious_Golf9014
selftext: Did anyone have any success with AI making good looking game UIs because all I ever got from AI looked like slop

replies.body: this, and also always show it references

replies.author: Prestigious_Golf9014

comments.author: Early_Flamingo5337
comments.body: I mean if you expect to write a couple of lines and make something great it just won't happen. You can develop any type of look but also have to put the hours and the work to describe and balance every single aspect of you want from it

comments.author: Used-Snow-9934
comments.body: I think the best way to go about this now is to stop promting for second.  You might lack the knowledge/skills to prompt and guide it properly.  Stop. Take some time to research it, gather reference of what you actually think a good UI is and what you think looks good. Break it down. Copy (and I don’t mean a rip off here) the things you like about it. Maybe you will find ways to improve it or tweak it to your game.

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body:
If you are using claude code, let it create artifacts.

Other than that, use any easy platform you like for building mockups (such as HTML, even if you're not making a browser game). Create a mockup you can interact with before you build a UI into the game and pick a framework for it.

UI design tools, like Figma, are going to struggle hard to stay relevant.

Furthermore ask yourself how much UI and what kind of UI controls you need. If your players don't necessarily have mouse and keyboard, make mouse navigation an add-on, and build it keyboard/controller first, using a minimal set of input actions. Don't build or use a whole window manager when you just need a few menus.

comments.author: qing-turn
comments.body:
What worked for me was splitting it into two separate jobs. First an image model makes a mockup of the whole screen in one consistent style (mine is a sticker-scrapbook look for a cat game), and I approve or reject those as pictures. Only after a mockup is approved does Claude rebuild it in the engine, with the mockup open next to it, then screenshot the real game and compare the two side by side. Asking a coding model to invent the look and build it at the same time is exactly where my slop came from.

  
The other thing that helped more than any prompt: cut text. My rule for the main screens is icon plus number, no explanations. A lot of AI UI looks like slop simply because it's crowded with labels.

comments.body: Generate the elements, the vision needs to be your own. Put them together yourself. Otherwise you're gonna get what looks like a barebones 90s web interface or overauthored web 2.0 junk.
